### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_date (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via invalid_date (literal, a string literal in validateOne))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75519e1c0a57b404de5e0d458f000817e3fb5dd8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5a9dfb31f96d241a9ff7fb23de2fa4df76855436` — the merge of head `6adb0dbbf169d5ccf6ddebdd2d965924226c1e38` into base `75519e1c0a57b404de5e0d458f000817e3fb5dd8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5a9dfb31f96d241a9ff7fb23de2fa4df76855436 && git checkout 5a9dfb31f96d241a9ff7fb23de2fa4df76855436
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 75519e1c0a57b404de5e0d458f000817e3fb5dd8 6adb0dbbf169d5ccf6ddebdd2d965924226c1e38 && git checkout -B drift-repro 75519e1c0a57b404de5e0d458f000817e3fb5dd8 && git merge --no-ff 6adb0dbbf169d5ccf6ddebdd2d965924226c1e38

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75519e1c0a57b404de5e0d458f000817e3fb5dd8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 75519e1c0a57b404de5e0d458f000817e3fb5dd8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6adb0dbbf169d5ccf6ddebdd2d965924226c1e38`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20846 (body and its four comments: triage `5910713137`, claim `5913951056`, `os-dev-report` `5920574465`, claim amendment `5920606351`), PR #20952 (body, 10-file list, net diff against `main`, mergeable clean), and the 35 check-runs on the head. Files at the head were read through `git show` on a fetched ref; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public surface, `@objectstack/core` root: one export added, `SUPPORTED_TEMPORAL_YEARS`.** Right. `packages/core/src/index.ts:113` is `export * from './utils/temporal-storage-form.js'`, so the constant reaches the `.` entry of the `exports` map (the only other entry is `./logger`). It is frozen at both levels and holds the same numbers the two private constants held (`date` 1 to 9999, `datetime` 1000 to 9999). `isOutsideTemporalYearRange` and `canonicalCalendarDay` read those same numbers, so core's own verdicts do not move; the new core test pins both edges inside, the years beside them outside, and the freeze. This is the one widening the diff publishes.
2. **Write door accept set (`validateRecord`, reached by `POST` / `PATCH /api/v1/data/:object` and each import row): unchanged.** Right. The guard `if (readable && !isUninterpretableTemporalComparand(t, value)) return null;` is untouched; every added line sits in the refusal branch and only picks a message key. The wire code stays `invalid_date` and `constraint` stays exactly `{ type }` (pinned with `toEqual` in the unit test and the REST pin), so the field-error payload does not widen, as the card's scope forbade. A number is never `readable`, so it keeps the ISO sentence (pinned as a control).
3. **Import reader accept set (`coerceFieldValue` / `coerceRow`): unchanged.** Right. `parseDateCell` is untouched; the new `outsideYears` is asked only inside the existing `d === undefined` branch and only changes the message key. The row's `code` stays `invalid_date` (as #20722 set it), `FieldCoerceError` is unchanged, and `coerceRow`, the only symbol from this module on rest's root entry (`packages/rest/src/index.ts:46`), keeps its signature. The sentence for a reader-refused cell in an out-of-range year moves from the import's own sentence to the kind's range sentence, so both refusal paths of one import give one sentence per kind. That matches the card's `reach:` line and the PR's H2.
4. **`@objectstack/spec` `./system`: the catalog `BUILTIN_VALIDATION_MESSAGES` gains `invalid_date_range` and `invalid_datetime_range` in `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES`.** Right, and not a published-surface widening: the const's declared type (a record of locale to a record of key to string) is unchanged, no export is added, and `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json` records export names only, so no generated baseline is owed (the check-run `Lint & Repo Gates` and the dev's `check:generated` agree). The keys are rendering variants of the existing `invalid_date` wire code, the same class as #20671's `invalid_time_zoned`. The catalog completeness test covers the four locales; the new spec test forbids any digit in the range templates, so the numbers have exactly one source. The four translations read correctly and each names the UTC year for `datetime`, which is what the predicate judges.
5. **`buildFieldError` gains an optional `messageParams` argument.** Not a public-surface change: objectql's `.` entry exports only `ValidationError`, `validateRecord`, `VALIDATION_FAILED_CODE` and types from the module (`index.ts:404` to `413`), and the lean `./core` entry only `ValidationError` and `validateRecord` (`core.ts:90` to `91`). Its spread order puts `messageParams` under `constraint` and `value`, so it can never shadow a shipped key. Right.
6. **Triage direction (`5910713137`), item by item.** One key per kind naming the range: met. Wire code stays and no key on `constraint`: met and pinned. Numbers from the same range function the doors use, no literal copy: met (both consumers read core's constant; the spec test forbids literals). Pins through `POST /api/v1/data/:object` and an import row, a readable `datetime` in year 0500 and a readable `date` in year 10000 getting the range sentence, a malformed value keeping the ISO sentence: met in `packages/rest/src/data-temporal-year-range-message.test.ts` over a real `SqlDriver` on SQLite (`0500-07-15T10:00:00Z`, `+010000-01-01`, the two malformed controls, and import rows r1, r2, r4, r5, plus the stored edges r6, r7). `PATCH` is not pinned by name; it runs the same validator arm, and the triage pins named `POST` and an import row, so no pin is owed.
7. **Serial constraint.** The card said after PR #20843; core at the head reads the `datetime` floor as 1000, the one that shipped. Met.
8. **Docs faces.** No page under `content/docs/**` or `apps/docs/**` names the keys or the sentences (zero hits at the head), so nothing is owed there; `Flag docs affected by code changes` is green.
9. **Check-runs on the head as the gate verdicts.** 35 check-runs: 31 `success`, 4 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in: path-filtered by the `filter` job), 0 failures. Green includes Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Lint & Repo Gates, the four Type Check jobs, the six Test Core shards, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), the three Dogfood shards and Dogfood Verify CLI, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, and the four claim and single-writer guards.

Non-blocking observations: the four-digit spelling of a year is written twice (`fourDigitYear` in objectql, an inline `padStart` in rest); that is a spelling rule, not a copy of the numbers, which have one source. The comparand door still spells its years as literals (the dev's own note); correct today and outside this card.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/20846-temporal-range-message.md`: `@objectstack/core` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/rest` patch. Right.
  - core minor: the diff adds one root export (item 1), and AGENTS.md's changeset rule reads "yes takes at least minor".
  - spec patch: a catalog gains two sentences under an unchanged type and no new export; the precedent `.changeset/20671-time-write-zone-less.md` graded the same class (`invalid_time_zoned`) as spec patch.
  - objectql and rest patch: a bug fix in a released package with no entry-point signature change and no accept-set move; never `skip-changeset`.
- Clause-②: `yes (widening)` on the PR body, in the changeset body, and in claim amendment `5920606351`. The three agree, and the arm is right: something is added, nothing is removed, and no value's verdict moves. No ADR-0087 marker is owed, since only a breaking changeset carries one.
- Changeset prose is accurate: the override advice names `validation.field.invalid_date_range` / `validation.field.invalid_datetime_range`, which matches `VALIDATION_MESSAGE_KEY_PREFIX` (`validation.field`) and the translate lookup in the catalog; the "what is not affected" paragraph matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the report: none. The five `deviations`, the two `out_of_scope_findings`, and the PR's four acceptance notes, each answered:

- **D1, landing site outside the claim (`packages/core/src/utils/temporal-storage-form.ts` and its test).** Accepted. Triage required the sentence's years to come from the range the doors use with no literal copy; the bounds were private module constants, so exporting them from their one producer was the only way to meet that without a second copy. Claim amendment `5920606351` extended the file surface to cover it.
- **D2, Clause-② declared `yes (widening)` instead of the claim's `no`.** Right, verified at item 1; the claim was amended in-thread to match.
- **D3, core graded minor where the dispatch expected patch.** Right, see ②.
- **D4, the shared `.git` deepened with a shallow-since fetch.** No contract bearing: an additive act on the dev's local clone, done so two derived gates could measure; nothing in the diff depends on it. Noted for the seat.
- **D5, resumed from `bee75cebe` rather than the dispatch's `9905e61c`.** No bearing: the PR is against `main`, mergeable clean at the head, and the check-runs measured the head against the current base.
- **O1 and acceptance note 1, the comparand door spells its years as literals.** Outside this card; correct today; drift risk only. Escalated to the seat as a candidate card, not blocking.
- **O2 and acceptance note 2, a non-ISO five-digit spelling is read in the host zone.** Not blocking: the verdict does not move on any host, only which of two true sentences is chosen for such a spelling; the pins use the ISO 8601 expanded spelling, which reads the same on every host.
- **Acceptance note 3, a value both malformed and out of range gets the range sentence.** Accepted: the sentence is true for that value, and the comparand door's `yearClassOf` orders the year class first the same way.
- **Acceptance note 4, overrides of `invalid_date` / `invalid_datetime` do not cover the new values.** Accepted: a rendering consequence of new keys, no wire change, stated in the changeset with the keys to define.
